_doc: The symbol surface between `ee.schimke.composeai.cli.serve` and the rest of the CLI.
A debt register for the preview-server split (issue #3824), not a config file: entries
only ever come off. `scripts/check-serve-seam.py` fails on a crossing that is not listed
(new coupling) AND on a listed entry that no longer crosses (prune it — that is progress).
Regenerate the shrunk list with `python3 scripts/check-serve-seam.py --write`.
cliInternalsUsedByServe: serve reaching into the CLI. Each entry is something the extracted
server would have to get from a published contract module instead. The bundle-format cluster
(BundleReader, BundleSigning, BundleClasspathHydration, extractBundle*, locateBundleSidecar*,
BUNDLE_VERSION, ZIP_DOS_EPOCH_MS) is #3824 preparation item 5 and is most of this list.
serveInternalsUsedByCli: the CLI reaching into serve. Each entry must either move to the
server build with serve, or move down into a contract module the CLI can keep using. The
long tail here is ServeCommand.kt, which #3824 wants reduced to a thin entry point.
forbiddenPackages is NOT a ratchet: an extracted preview server never imports a renderer, an
forbiddenPackages is NOT a ratchet: an extracted preview server never imports a renderer, an
MCP server, or the gradle plugin, and there is nothing here to grandfather. `…composeai.plugin`
is the plugin's real namespace (`plugin`, `plugin.daemon`, `plugin.tooling`) — an earlier
`…composeai.gradle` entry named nothing at all and enforced nothing, while `plugin.tooling`
types sit on the CLI compile classpath via `:gradle-preview-driver`, ready to be reached for.
contractPackages maps each non-`cli` package serve imports to the module that publishes
it, and must agree with `contracts` in preview-server/contract-probe/build.gradle.kts —
that is what stops a hand-maintained coordinate list from silently missing a module serve
has started using. unpublishedContracts records a mapped module that cannot be resolved
as an artifact yet; each one is a split blocker, not an exemption.
unpublishedContracts records a mapped module that cannot be resolved as an artifact yet;
each one is a split blocker, not an exemption. It is empty today: every module serve
imports from is published. `daemon.bta` maps to `daemon-core`, not to `:daemon:bta-host` —
the package is declared by BOTH modules and the types serve uses (BtaCompileSession,
DiagnosticCollector) are the `daemon-core` ones. A package name is not a module name; the
test asserts each mapping against the module that actually declares the imported type.
reflectiveDependencies records a module serve reaches by class name in a string literal:
subprocess main classes and classloader-loaded sidecars. No import scan can see one, and
the contract probe cannot either, because it never stages them. This is the one category
where these checks are blind by construction, so the register is manual, pinned by a test
that each literal still exists, and guarded by a test that finds unrecorded ones. Two of
the four are unpublished modules — the real split blockers, in place of the one this PR
first reported wrongly.

ee.schimke.composeai.usagepsi.UsageSourc.why: The playground's source cleaner loads :usage-source-psi in an isolated classloader and calls one String->JSON method. It degrades: absent, the cleaner falls back to its text passes, so an extracted server without it loses parse-quality cleaning rather than breaking. Staged by cli/build.gradle.kts through the composePreviewUsagePsi configuration.

ee.schimke.composeai.rcembedded.jvm.RcJv.why: Subprocess main class for the embedded Remote Compose player. #3824 already lists this module among the sidecars the CLI tarball stages; it is an in-repo project dependency today and would have to become a published artifact for the split.
The worker-pool half of the same sidecar.

ee.schimke.composeai.daemon.DaemonMain.why: Main class of the daemon JVM serve spawns for a bundle. A process-launch string, not a compile dependency — serve never links against a daemon implementation, and checkCliDaemonLibraryBoundary still forbids it on the classpath. Both modules are published, so this is staging rather than a blocker.
